gen-fs-excon-gf-montagu-slab: Montagu Slab sets down classic serif contrast, gentle and subdued. Excon is best at crowded, chalk-mark strokes with no contrast at all, while Montagu Slab is best at sturdy downstrokes and slender turns.
gen-fs-excon-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana: Crowded chalk marks from Excon, then Noto Serif Hentaigana below, its small letters nearly capital height with open jaws on curves. Single-width pen line against modulated strokes is the real hook.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-cutive: Modern and chain-linked, New Title stands tall in the lowercase while Cutive spreads wide tracking and an open c. Give Cutive a little extra size so its tracking breathes.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-habibi: Modern, New Title locks tall lowercase letters together like chain links. Habibi is a text serif, its clear channel leading into each round letter, and it can take a slightly larger size.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-inika: Letters locked like chain links define New Title. New Title is best at tall, bold display lowercase, while Inika, a text serif, is best at see-through gaps in each s.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-kay-pho-du: New Title is bold and modern, its lowercase tall and its letters locked like links in a fine chain. And Kay Pho Du follows with breathing counters, a serif that reads gently down a page.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-labrada: Labrada is dignified and bookish, opening its small letters wide. Under New Title, whose tall lowercase is locked link to link, it settles the page into a quieter rhythm.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-laila: Generous space between curve ends and stems gives an editorial, traditional reading texture. Laila meets New Title, whose tall, chain-linked lowercase makes the height difference the standout quality of the pair.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-rhodium-libre: New Title is bold and modern, its lowercase standing tall and its letters locked like chain links. But Rhodium Libre lifts its brush ends away before each curve closes, keeping the text traditional underneath.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-bespoke-serif: Bespoke Serif reads with authority, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones. And across a stretch it keeps a dignified, taffy-soft swell in each curve, well away from Oswald.
